1.explanation: All of the listed patterns and grammar definitions control how Prism detects Java class names. The clike definition’s 'class-name' token and Java’s classNamePrefix and className regexes determine which identifiers get tagged as class names. Currently the regex for className only matches identifiers containing at least one lowercase letter or single-letter names, so all-uppercase acronyms like UUID don’t fit the pattern and aren’t tokenized. Adjusting these regexes (in classNamePrefix/className and/or the class-name tokens in the extend/insertBefore calls) will allow UUID and other uppercase-only class names to be recognized and highlighted correctly.
1.bug_scenario: When highlighting Java code with Prism on the HackerTalk editor, the import statement “import java.util.UUID;” renders “UUID” as plain text instead of a class-name token. The screenshot shows that built-in types like String or Pattern are correctly highlighted, but the all-caps acronym “UUID” is not recognized by the Java grammar and is left unstyled.

2.explanation: Prism’s Java grammar defines a RegExp (in the variable className) that only matches class names starting with an uppercase letter followed by at least one lowercase letter. As a result, identifiers composed entirely of uppercase letters (like “UUID”) don’t satisfy the pattern and aren’t tokenized as “class-name”. The key code to fix is the className pattern in components/prism-java.js (and by extension its use inside Prism.languages.java) so that it accepts all-uppercase identifiers as valid class names.
2.bug_scenario: In the Java editor on HackerTalk, the import line “import java.util.UUID;” renders “UUID” as plain text rather than as a class-name token. On GitHub’s highlighter you can see “UUID” styled like other class names, but Prism’s Java grammar fails to recognize all-uppercase acronyms (no lowercase letters) as valid class names.
